messages:
kayla_cs: Lumenly reporting 429s during their midnight canary in eu-west. Spike ~380 clients in ~20s, mostly at app cold-start.

kayla_cs: They sent a sample fail: ```POST /v1/sdk/init HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
x-request-id: lum-1122
Response: 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 13
```

lumenly-ops: We're using the browser SDK in an edge worker pool. Current bootstrap: `Redwood.init({ envKey: 'pk_live_lumen', ephemeralTTL: 15, prefetch: true })`. Edge header at failure: `x-active-sockets: 392`.

tess_sdk: Looks like a classic validation stampede—many short TTLs + no startup jitter + prefetch = bad combo. Quick guidance: increase ephemeralTTL to 180-300s, disable prefetch for the canary, and add a small randomized splay on startup (200-800ms).

omar_eng: Also ask them to enable connection reuse on the worker (keepalive/http2) so init calls don't spawn new TLS handshakes. Example patch: ```// edge worker snippet
fetch('/v1/sdk/init', { keepalive: true, headers: { Connection: 'keep-alive' } })```

infra-juno: Infra traces show auth validation QPS jump for lumenly account and a short auth queue backlog. Short-term mitigation: we can enable per-account token coalescing to dedupe identical validations within a 10s window. I can scope a flag for 15 minutes.

onboard-bot: Ticket created: CS-#6120 "Lumenly init 429s (canary)". Assigned to omar_eng, infra-juno. Playbook: https://confluence.redwood/integration-playbooks/bootstrapping-backpressure (internal).

lumenly-ops: We'll change TTL to 240 and put a 200-600ms jitter in the canary at 5% -> 20% -> 100%. Starting canary now and holding at 5% for 3m.

tess_sdk: If 429s persist after those changes, ask for two failing `x-request-id` values and a snapshot of `x-active-sockets` + `x-client-conns`. We'll correlate to auth queue traces and consider temporary per-account burst smoothing.

infra-juno: Flag toggled for lumenly account; monitoring. Posting back in ~10m.

kayla_cs: I'll update the customer health note and check back once the canary finishes. Please send any `x-request-id` if failures continue.

lumenly-ops: Can confirm canary rolled with TTL=240 and jitter. Will report status in 10m. Thanks! :pray:
